name: Diphenhydramine
executiveSummary: First-generation H1 antihistamine. Adult: **25–50 mg PO/IV/IM every 6–8 h** (usual max **300–400 mg/day**). Pediatrics: **1–2 mg/kg/dose every 6–8 h** (max **50 mg**/dose; ~**5 mg/kg/day**). Sedating; not in neonates.
indications:
## Indications

- Allergic reactions, pruritus, urticaria; anaphylaxis adjunct (after epinephrine).
- Selected nausea/vomiting; sedation / premedication.
- Acute dystonia from neuroleptics (alternative to biperiden per protocol).

## Precautions

- Strong anticholinergic: glaucoma, urinary retention, ileus, myasthenia.
- Sedation and paradoxical excitation in infants. **Do not use in neonates**; caution <6 months.
- Avoid in acute asthma crisis as bronchodilator monotherapy.

> IV: dilute and infuse ~15 min; no rapid bolus.

adulto.dose: **25–50 mg every 6–8 h** PO/IV/IM. Usual max **300–400 mg/day**. Premedication/anaphylaxis adjunct: **25–50 mg** IV/IM.
adulto.administration: PO with food. IV: dilute in NS/D5W; ~15 min. Deep IM.

pediatrico.presentation: Syrup 2.5 mg/mL; tabs 50 mg; ampoule 10 mg/mL.
pediatrico.dose: **1–2 mg/kg/dose every 6–8 h** (**~3–5 mg/kg/day**; max **50 mg**/dose). Premedication: **1 mg/kg** (max **50 mg**).
pediatrico.notes: <6 months: possible paradoxical excitation. Not neonates.

stability:
## Stability

- Opened ampoule: discard leftover per card.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Sedation, dry mouth, urinary retention, blurred vision, tachycardia, hypotension; anticholinergic overdose (delirium, seizures).
